message.content:
Below are several ways—depending on your operating system, whether you’re looking at a **local** interface or querying a **remote** device—to pull out all of the “detailed” data that most people consider part of an interface’s profile. | Goal | Typical Command / Tool | What it shows | |------|------------------------|---------------| | **Local host – basic config & state** | `ip addr show dev `
`ifconfig ` | Interface name, MTU, flags (UP/DOWN), IPv4/IPv6 addresses, broadcast/multicast groups | | **Link‑layer stats** | `cat /sys/class/net//statistics/*`
`netstat -i ` | RX/TX packets, errors, drops, collisions | | **Hardware capabilities** | `ethtool ` | Speed, duplex, autonegotiation, supported modes, driver version | | **Detailed hardware description** | `sudo lshw -C network -short` | Driver/module, bus info, physical location, vendor ID | | **Remote device via SSH/SCP** | `ssh admin@router "show interfaces "` | Vendor‑specific output (Cisco IOS, Juniper JUNOS, Arista EOS) | | **SNMP walk** | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public IF-MIB::ifTable` | OIDs covering speed, mtu, operStatus, physAddress, etc. | | **RESTful APIs (e.g., NETCONF/Restconf)** | `curl -k https://device/api/interfaces/` | Structured JSON/YAML describing configuration/state | --- ### Quick Reference Cheat Sheet #### Linux / Unix ```bash # Basic interface list + state $ ip link show # or: $ ifconfig -a # Detailed per-interface view $ ip addr show dev eth0 $ ethtool eth0 # requires root privileges $ cat /sys/class/net/eth0/statistics/rx_packets ``` #### macOS ```bash $ ifconfig en0 # replace en0 with your iface $ netstat -I en0 $ sysctl hw.network.en0.macaddr ``` #### Windows (PowerShell) ```powershell # List adapters Get-NetAdapter # Full detail for one adapter (Get-NetAdapter -Name Ethernet0).InterfaceDescription, (Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias Ethernet0), (Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix 0.0.0.0/0) ``` #### Remote Devices (via CLI) *Example: Cisco IOS* ```text Router# show interfaces GigabitEthernet0/1 GigabitEthernet0/1 is up, line protocol is up Hardware is iGbE, address is 00aa.bbcc.dddd (bia 00aa.bbcc.dddd) Internet address is 192.168.10.1/24 MTU 1500 bytes, BW 100000 Kbit/sec, DLY 1000 usec ... ``` *Example: Juniper JUNOS* ```text root@juniper# show interfaces ge-0/0/1 terse ge-0/0/1 { unit 0 { family inet { address 172.16.5.1/30; } } } ``` #### Using SNMP ```bash snmpwalk -v2c -c community_string hostname IF-MIB::ifDescr snmpwalk -v2c -c community_string hostname IF-MIB::ifOperStatus ``` These commands return values such as *up*, *down*, *testing*, etc. --- ### When You Need Even More Detail Sometimes you’ll want to dig into firmware settings, QoS policies, VLAN tagging, or security features. In those cases look for: | Feature | How to access | |---------|--------------| | **VLANs** | `bridge vlan show dev ` (Linux); `switchport mode trunk` (IOS) | | **QoS marks** | `tc qdisc ls dev ` (Linux); `policy-map type qos` (IOS) | | **Security ACLs** | `iptables -L INPUT -n --line-numbers` (Linux); `access-list` (IOS) | | **Driver diagnostics** | `modprobe -r ; modprobe debug=...` (Linux) | --- ### Common Pitfalls 1. **Permissions:** Many commands (`ethtool`, reading `/sys/...`) require super‑user rights. 2. **Multiple NICs:** If you have bonded/slave interfaces, check both master and slave configs. 3. **Virtual Interfaces:** Docker bridges, VPN tunnels, or virtual NICs may hide real traffic metrics unless explicitly queried. 4. **Vendor-Specific Extensions:** Some devices expose proprietary MIB objects or CLI options beyond standard ones. --- ### TL;DR To fetch *all* available details for an interface: 1. Identify the platform (Linux/macOS/Windows). 2. Run the appropriate native utility (`ip`, `ifconfig`, `ethtool`, `Get-NetAdapter`, etc.). 3. For deeper inspection, combine multiple sources: statistics files, driver reports, and vendor-specific CLI/API calls. 4. If the target is remote, either SSH into the device or issue SNMP/REST queries against its management plane. Feel free to let me know which OS or device you’re working with, and I can tailor the exact set of commands!
